commenter_information.author_organization_name: American Immunization Registry Association (AIRA); American Medical Informatics Association (AMIA); Association of Public Health Laboratories (APHL); Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO); Big Cities Health Coalition (BCHC); Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists (CSTE); Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS); National Association of County and City Health Officials (NACCHO); Public Health Informatics Institute (PHII)
commenter_information.stakeholder_type: Professional Association / Public Health Advocacy Group
commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: Coalition of public health informatics and public health organizations focused on health IT, public health infrastructure, surveillance, and care coordination.

executive_summary: The coalition supports CMS and ONC efforts to improve standards-based interoperability and the usefulness of electronic event notifications for care coordination. The comment focuses on the RFI for electronic event notifications, recommending use of public health ADT/syndromic surveillance experience, pilots and incentives before expanding recipients, and stronger data quality testing and validation.

standards_referenced: PHIN Messaging Guide for Syndromic Surveillance

detailed_positions.topic: Use public health ADT and syndromic surveillance experience to improve event notifications
detailed_positions.rationale: Syndromic surveillance reporting already uses ADT-like messages with additional data elements important for public health surveillance and may inform what data would improve care coordination.
detailed_positions.specific_request: CMS should explore the PHIN syndromic surveillance messaging guide and related ADT-like public health reporting experience when considering additional event notification elements.

detailed_positions.topic: Expand event notification recipients cautiously through pilots and stakeholder input
detailed_positions.rationale: Additional provider types may benefit from notifications, but CMS should first determine whether ADT messages are sufficient and what additional elements are needed for different care settings.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Conduct surveys and pilots, potentially with incentives and networks such as TEFCA/HIEs, before requiring hospitals to send alerts to provider types beyond current regulation.

detailed_positions.rationale: ADT feeds may be hindered by inconsistent standardization and variable data quality; real-world testing and validation would improve utility while reducing burden if metrics are calculated by CEHRT or centralized dashboards.
detailed_positions.specific_request: CMS should work with ONC on real-world onboarding and production validation, consider incentives tied to priority data elements, create processes for serious data quality remediation, and evaluate numerator/denominator metrics and centralized dashboards.

solicitation_responses.solicitation: RFI: Electronic Event Notifications for Value-Based Care and Care Coordination
solicitation_responses.summary: The commenters respond to the RFI by recommending additional standardized data elements, careful expansion of recipient types, pilots, TEFCA/HIE incentives, and stronger testing and data quality validation.

key_quotes: We applaud CMS and ONC on their efforts to further an interoperable health technology ecosystem rooted in standards-based data exchange.
Use of ADT feeds to improve patient care may be hindered by lack of standardization and variable data quality.
agency_action_requested: Consider public health messaging guides and data-quality infrastructure when developing event notification policy; use pilots, incentives, validation, and stakeholder surveys before expanding regulatory requirements.
